prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop visual-direction comp for a Rust quantitative research documentation website
Primary request: Design the first viewport of Helios Alpha as an Annotated Event Atlas, where rare-event research reads as evidence plates and every claim is attached to an exact observation.
Scene/backdrop: a bright, contemporary quantitative research notebook translated into a web interface.
Subject: one large aligned-time event-study plot centered at t=0, transparent comparison overlays, precise marginal annotations, compact state/replay metadata, and a small typed Rust composition excerpt.
Style/medium: premium editorial web UI comp, scientific atlas fused with an interactive statistical notebook.
Composition/framing: 16:10 landscape desktop viewport, restrained navigation, the plot dominates, annotations live in ruled margins, no generic feature-card grid.
Lighting/mood: rigorous, calm, inspectable, research-grade.
Color palette: cool white #f5f7f4, ink #111b24, indigo #3155a6, oxide #c64a2e, acid chartreuse #b7d93d used sparingly.
Materials/textures: vellum overlays, registration marks, ruled annotation margins, technical ink.
Text (verbatim): "HELIOS ALPHA", "ANNOTATED EVENT ATLAS", "ALIGNED TIME", "t = 0", "REPLAYABLE STATE", "SYNTHETIC DATA"
Constraints: desktop website comp only; plot labels must be credible and legible; accessible contrast; no logo; no watermark.
Avoid: academic PDF facsimile, dark trading terminal, candlestick charts, generic SaaS cards, beige nostalgia, gratuitous gradients, photographic people.
